Trail of the Week: Ross Creek Cedars – Wild Montana

Tucked in northwest Montana, the Ross Creek Cedars Scenic Area offers a magical winter escape. Massive western red cedars rise above peaceful snow-covered trails, inviting snowshoers to explore one of the region’s most awe-inspiring old-growth forests. Beneath their sweeping branches, the hush of falling snow creates a timeless, cathedral-like stillness. 

To learn more about Ross Creek Cedars Trail and Wild Montana’s work protecting wild places, visit hikewildmontana.org.


Trail Details

Total distance: .8 miles
Elevation gain: 100 feet
Highest elevation: 2,867 feet
Nearest town: Libby
How to get there →

How to Hike Kind on Montana’s Trails

Montana can feel like a small town, with a friend and a smile around every bend in the trail. Kindness is the key to keeping this friendly vibe under the Big Sky. No matter where you live or how you recreate, these Hike Kind tips can help create a culture of kindness outdoors. When we play responsibly, we’re kind to ourselves, the wildlands we love, and our community. Learn more →

Giant Cedars Boardwalk Trail - Vancouver to the Rockies, Canada

Giant Cedars Boardwalk Trail

HikeSightseeing

17

Directions

Gemma, Off Track TravelVancouver to the Rockies Travel Guide

The best place to stretch your legs between Golden and Revelstoke is the short Giant Cedars Boardwalk Trail.

This easy 500m loop path leads into the heart of the forest in Mount Revelstoke National Park. It has some lovely stretches of boardwalk through old growth trees. There are picnic tables in the parking area.

A valid Parks Canada day pass is required - $22/vehicle with up to 7 people.

Helpful info on parks.canada.ca
